rejected.reason: These are not stale. The round builds one identity of each test binary per feature unit (89 exe names hold 10 to 16 identities), and 41.86 GiB were written by attempt 2's canary as warm state for attempt 3. Dropping them repeats what plan S caused: attempt 2 had to rebuild them (32.8 to 96.2 GiB, cause_reading in round-R60.json). The 9.70 GiB written before attempt 2 are copies superseded only by mtime in their name group; which of them the round will not rebuild is unknown without the round's unit hashes (N3). The tool would accept this path (round owner, no status check), so it is rejected here by judgement, not by the tool.
